hypothesis: A request held in a user-space TCP proxy can remain pending after the local X11 owner process retires; the X server may reject the bytes after resource disconnection or process them as a late global input.
discriminator: Compare proxy delivery_forwarded/client_to_server_error timestamps with cancellation terminal completion and owner retirement, plus old-task count, fresh-task contamination, and independent keymap reads.

condition.display: parent :88 Unix socket; runtime owner 127.0.0.1:89 TCP proxy

stop_rule: One run only; no retry. Preserve any setup/runtime/assertion failure. Keep separate from server-side XTEST R01-R21 and from R10-R17 statistics.
interpretation: This intentionally delays bytes at a user-space relay before Xvfb TCP receive. It is not natural packet loss/latency or WSLc. Finite recovery is not promoted from a green test alone; task effect, server-side disconnect, release proof and UNKNOWN/replay fence all remain separate gates.
scope: Synthetic app in private Xvfb, cached Docker image, no model/provider, no external network.
